overview: The Ayutthaya Kingdom was a major Southeast Asian power that controlled much of the mainland and engaged in vast international trade. Its cosmopolitan capital hosted merchants from Japan, Persia and Europe, while its kings adopted the divine devaraja concept.

items.text: International trade with China, Japan, India, Persia, Portugal and the Dutch Republic.
The capital hosted foreign merchant quarters with Japanese, Chinese, Persian and European communities.
Rice, sugar, tin, timber and animal products exported in large quantities.
Temple architecture with tall prang towers and elaborate gilded decoration.
Thai literature and poetry developed in the royal court.
Theravada Buddhism received royal patronage with hundreds of temples built.
The Khmer devaraja concept of divine kingship adopted and adapted.
Ayutthaya Historical Park is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
Thai political and cultural traditions established during this period continue today.

fall.text: The Burmese sacked and destroyed the city, though Siam was quickly reunified under King Taksin.
